- Outer cortex showing browning and rot

## Analysis Summary

**Test image features:**
- Two tomato stems with root systems pulled from soil, laid against white background
- Internal brown/tan vascular streaking visible through the stem surface (lower portions)
- Cortex partially damaged/stripped revealing cream-tan interior with brown vascular discoloration
- Brown, fibrous dead roots
- Upper stems still green — disease progressing from roots upward

**Reference comparisons:**
- **Bacterial_Wilt** (Bugwood_3): Showed cross-section with identical internal brown vascular discoloration (bacterial ooze test) — strongest visual match for the vascular browning pattern
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: All three references showed leaf symptoms only (yellowing, marginal browning) — no stem/root match
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Showed ooze test, different presentation
- **Southern_Blight**: White mycelium present — absent in test image
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Leaf symptoms only

**Conclusion:** The extensive internal vascular browning extending from the roots up through the lower stem is the hallmark of bacterial wilt. The diagnostic presentation (stems pulled and examined on white background) and the pattern of discoloration match the Bacterial_Wilt reference most closely. Verticillium Wilt is the main alternative, but its reference images showed leaf symptoms and it causes more gradual, patterned discoloration rather than this extensive root-to-stem browning.
